issues.detail: Repeat diastolic readings are 104 and 102 mm Hg. The fact record says to avoid diastolic values of 101-109 because the ADA table is internally inconsistent (body: 100-109 emergency band; footnote: diastolic >100 = refer as soon as possible / urgent evaluation if symptomatic). A student can defend 'refer' from the footnote.
issues.suggestion: Use diastolic values under 100 (e.g., 168/96 and 166/94) so only the systolic 160-180 band applies, and update the explanation.

issues.detail: The stem sentence 'Urgent pain needs treatment' hands over the pathway, and C is the only option that says treat and monitor. D ('ignore the pain') and B (120/80 for an infection) are implausible, so a test-wise student gets it without knowing the ADA band.
issues.suggestion: Drop the first stem sentence (the box already shows pain/swelling); make distractors realistic, e.g. 'Defer all care and refer to the physician today' and 'Treat only after BP is below 140/90'.

issues.detail: Option A uses an absolute ('unmonitored') and D mixes two ideas (180/110 threshold plus ignoring pain), making them easy to rule out.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite D as a single plausible error, e.g. 'Defer treatment because BP exceeds 140/90'.

issues.detail: 'What A1C threshold meets the laboratory criterion for diabetes?' - options B, C and D all meet the criterion (D's own why line says it 'also indicates diabetes'). Only the lowest cutoff is meant, and the stem never says 'lowest' or 'diagnostic cutoff'.
issues.suggestion: Reword: 'What is the lowest A1C value that meets the diagnostic criterion for diabetes?'

issues.detail: The item ignores the case-set patient (already diagnosed, A1C 7.4%); it is a pure recall item with no link to the box, and 7.4% in the box makes 7.0% a tempting but irrelevant cue.
issues.suggestion: Tie it to the patient (e.g., what 7.4% means for control vs diagnosis) or move it out of the case set.

issues.detail: Level 1 recall with the case box adds nothing; check the CC/phase tags (phase dx) fit a patient already treated with insulin.
issues.suggestion: Retag or standalone.

issues.detail: The case-set patient box is a 67-year-old male, but the stem (and explanation) say 'she/her'.
issues.suggestion: Use 'he' in the stem and 'his' in the explanation.

issues.detail: C is the longest and most specific option (amount, timing). Distractor A (withhold carbohydrate for potassium) is implausible and B/D both end 'continue the appointment', which is a visible cue for wrong.
issues.suggestion: Make A realistic (e.g., 'Give 15 to 20 g of orange juice, then recheck in 15 minutes' is arguably a trap worth testing given CKD) and vary the endings.

issues.detail: Explanation says to choose gel rather than orange juice for CKD, but no option involves juice, so the CKD teaching point is not tested.
issues.suggestion: Add a juice option or drop that sentence from the explanation.

issues.detail: The case-set patient box is a 67-year-old male, but the stem (and explanation) say 'she/her'.
issues.suggestion: Use 'he'.

issues.detail: Option A (gel between cheek and gum) is a real buccal-gel practice that some sources use in a drowsy patient; the item relies on 'nothing by mouth' without saying the patient is at aspiration risk beyond 'cannot swallow safely'. It is the only plausible distractor.
issues.suggestion: Reword A as 'Orange juice by mouth' or 'Glucose tablets under the tongue', or state in the stem that he is obtunded and cannot protect his airway.

issues.detail: B (more insulin) and D (water) are absurd and the stem's 'glucose-raising' phrase eliminates both; effectively a 2-option item. Key also carries dose and route (most specific).
issues.suggestion: Replace B and D with plausible dental-office options (e.g., 'IV dextrose via IV access' only if appropriate, 'Epinephrine 0.3 mg IM', 'Albuterol inhaler').

issues.detail: Glucagon route is not given in C (IM/SC per label) although 1 mg is stated; stem does not say help is already called vs. being called, which collides with R05.
issues.suggestion: State 'Glucagon 1 mg IM' and make EMS timing consistent across R04/R05.

issues.detail: Sequence contradiction with R04 (which says help is being called) and with the source (call EMS immediately for severe hypoglycemia). R05 treats 'Call EMS' as a new action 15 minutes later, teaching that EMS can wait; and key D hedges 'if needed' while the stem already states no response.
issues.suggestion: Make R05 about the repeat dose / airway and monitoring while EMS is en route; key e.g. 'Give a second equal glucagon dose and keep monitoring until EMS arrives'.

issues.detail: A (wait without seeking help), B (juice while unable to swallow) and C (resume treatment) are all clearly unsafe and are contradicted by R04, so D is the only sensible choice without any knowledge of the repeat-dose rule.
issues.suggestion: Use plausible distractors, e.g. 'Give 2 mg glucagon (double dose)', 'Give oral glucose gel buccally', 'Wait 30 minutes before repeating', 'Give IV insulin'.

issues.detail: The case-set patient box is a 67-year-old male, but the stem (and explanation) say 'she/her'.
issues.suggestion: Use 'he'.

issues.detail: B is the only option that is a real clinical-history answer; A (age only), C (tooth number) and D (morning appointment) are absurd, and B is the longest and a generic list ('control, recent care, medicines, function'). A student passes with no ASA knowledge. The item does not test ASA classification at all.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite as 'What ASA status best describes this patient?' with the box supplying COPD, exertional dyspnea after one flight, and a recent hospital visit, options ASA II/III/IV/V, key ASA III (or clarify the hospitalization to justify IV).

issues.detail: Cited ASA-2/3/4 records list class examples; none supports 'review disease control, recent care, medicines, function' as the keyed content.
issues.suggestion: Cite the ASA statement text that fits the rewritten question.

issues.detail: 'Medicines' is already fully listed in the box, so 'additional history' about medicines is redundant; 'additional history' is undefined.
issues.suggestion: Remove the 'clarify' framing.

issues.detail: Chief complaint is medical, not a dental complaint, for a dental patient box.
issues.suggestion: Use a dental complaint and move dyspnea to history.

issues.detail: Explanation says 'Her controlled hypertension', but the box shows BP 166/96 on repeat (and R08 treats it as above the ADA threshold). Hypertension is not controlled here, so the rationale contradicts the box.
issues.suggestion: Say 'hypertension that is not currently controlled' or change the box; better, ask the ASA class (ASA III for uncontrolled HTN plus prosthetic valve).

issues.detail: A ('Ignore'), B ('stand-alone prediction') and C ('solely') are absolute/extreme wording, while D is the hedged, balanced, longest option. Answerable by style alone; the item tests a generic principle, not ASA knowledge.
issues.suggestion: Make distractors moderate and concrete, or convert to 'What ASA class fits this patient?' with options II-V.

issues.detail: D ('plan from function and clinical details') is vague; the ASA statement itself says only that the class describes physical status, so 'best' rests on subjective phrasing.
issues.suggestion: Anchor the key to the ASA statement (class does not predict operative risk).

issues.detail: Phase 'clear' and cognitive level 2 do not match a definition-recall item.
issues.suggestion: Retag.

issues.detail: The box gives a 3-day chewing pain with a tooth planned for extraction, yet the stem declares the extraction 'elective'. By R01's own logic, pain-driven urgent care at 160-180 systolic follows the emergency pathway (option A), so a defensible reading conflicts with the keyed answer; the explanation's 'no acute infection' is not in the stem.
issues.suggestion: Change the chief complaint to a non-urgent one (e.g., 'I want this broken tooth taken out', no pain) or state no pain/infection in the box.

issues.detail: The stem states 'repeat systolic above 160' and names the ADA guide, so the numeric rule can be applied without the box.
issues.suggestion: Give the actual readings in the stem or leave them to the box.

issues.detail: The answer is in the box verbatim ('Transcatheter prosthetic aortic valve') and the three distractors are non-cardiac or irrelevant lines pulled from the same box (activity level, hypertension, caries). No realistic confounder (coronary stent, pacemaker, mitral valve prolapse, rheumatic disease) is tested.
issues.suggestion: Use cardiac distractors, e.g. coronary stent, pacemaker, mitral valve prolapse, and keep the valve in the box.

issues.detail: Cognitive level 2 is generous for simple recall of a listed category.
issues.suggestion: Retag level 1 or add application.

issues.detail: B and D fail mainly on timing and do not test drug choice; only A tests the clindamycin change. Consider an allergy-appropriate cephalexin/doxycycline-before-treatment option as a distractor.
issues.suggestion: Optional: replace D with 'Cephalexin 30 to 60 minutes before treatment'.
